source: Exploration reference values (NASA JSC-67378 Rev 1; NASA-STD-3001 Vol 2 Rev F)

items.label: Food energy
items.value_text: Crew average of about 3,035 kcal per day, plus 200 kcal per hour of EVA. A population average, not a personal target.

items.label: Protein
items.unit: g per kg body mass per day
items.value_text: 1.2 to 1.8 g per kg of body mass per day.

items.label: Drinking fluid
items.value_text: 32 mL per kg of body mass, and no less than 2500 mL for men and 2100 mL for women per day.
items.sex_note: The rule uses the women's value because crew sex is not recorded.
items.source_ref: NASA JSC-67378 Rev 1, p. 3 and Table 1

items.label: Sodium
items.source_ref: NASA JSC-67378 Rev 1, p. 6 and Table 1

items.label: Potassium
items.value_text: 3400 mg per day for men and 2600 mg per day for women.
items.sex_note: Differs by sex; not judged because sex is not recorded.

items.label: Calcium
items.value_text: 1000 to 1200 mg per day, and no more than 2500 mg per day.
items.source_ref: NASA JSC-67378 Rev 1, p. 6 and Table 1

items.label: Iron
items.value_text: No more than 8 mg per day.
items.sex_note: Women under 50 who do not suppress menstruation have a different reference that is not judged here.
items.source_ref: NASA JSC-67378 Rev 1, p. 6 and Table 1

notes: These are population references from NASA documents, not a personal target.
JSC-67378 is a NASA program document, not NASA-STD-3001; vitamin D and the energy average come from NASA-STD-3001.

Sodium, iron, fluid, vitamin D and calcium were re-read in the documents by the Science review (M1). The energy, protein, carbohydrate, fat and potassium entries come from the planning text and were not re-read there yet.
No energy rule is written: the equation constant is printed differently in JSC-67378 (622) and NASA-STD-3001 Table 7.1-1 (662).
